options.consequence: a consumer that needs both PageScope and ModuleScopeObserver knows to wait on both nidana.flutter.5 and .6, or on .7; the three produced-by-phase contracts read alike

The same edit names nidana.flutter.7 as the phase that binds navigation-api@v1's executor suite. decisions.question: Step 6: are the four amends (G5 and G6 off-type values through a widened subscription; G7 a route named / gives /; G8 binding kept across a bus change; G17 one publisher per topic with a writer per type argument and ClaimRejected) backward-compatible, so they apply within v1, or could any break a consumer and go to the owner with a version bump?

options.label: all four compatible, apply within v1
options.consequence: G5, G6, G7, G8, G17 and the PageScope and stub comments gain the clauses, a Versioning line records the amendment; no version bump

options.label: one or more breaking, stop for the owner and bump to v2
options.consequence: a v2 for a contract with no implementation, whose only consumer (nidana.integration) is unplanned and whose fixtures never exercised the changed cases

decisions.chosen: all four compatible, apply within v1
decisions.why: No declaration changes and no stated behavior is weakened. G5 and G6 stated nothing for an off-type value, which bus-api@v1 G41 as amended now makes possible. G7 as written gave a route named / the empty route, which PageSource's non-empty assertion rejects, so no conforming outcome existed. G8's 'binds once' already reads as the amend. G17's 'same writer on every call' cannot hold across two type arguments (F5: the cached writer fails the cast), and one publisher per topic keeps bus-api@v1 G20's one claim, as bus-testing@v1 G18 does. No fixture of any contract exercised any changed case, and the 52 pre-amendment cases and the 26 executor-suite cases pass against a stand-in that meets all four (T7). Each falls under the Versioning list's 'a new guarantee that existing fixtures still pass'. G7 is the closest: if an adopter had already keyed sources on a route named / failing to mount, it would change; none can exist before the package does.

decisions.question: ADR-001 item 3 coverage of the amended clauses: add behavior cases now (S34 recommended G5/G6 and G17, G7 and G8 optional), add only the recommended ones, or record not-executable lines naming nidana.flutter's gates and schedule an hsdd-contract step?

options.label: five cases: G5, G6, G7, G8, G17
options.consequence: about 150 lines of fixture; the suite goes from 52 to 57 cases; every amended clause has a case that fails when the clause is broken; no follow-up hsdd-contract step

options.label: three cases: G5, G6, G17
options.consequence: the recommended set; the G7 root-route rule and the G8 bus-change rule stay covered only by the guarantee's older cases, which do not exercise them

options.label: not-executable lines and a later hsdd-contract step
options.consequence: no fixture work now, but clauses that are cheap to execute stay unchecked and the orchestrator must schedule another step

decisions.chosen: five cases: G5, G6, G7, G8, G17
decisions.why: Each case is small (15 to 35 lines) and settled by S34's stand-in, so the step's 'same edit if small' instruction applies. Confirmed in the experiment: on the stand-in as copied, the new G5, G6, G7 and G17 cases fail and every other case passes (T4); on the stand-in patched to meet the amendments every case of both bindings passes, 57 and 26 (T5); a seeded PageScope that rebinds on a bus change fails the new G8 case and no other (T6); each consuming gate's --guarantee prefix selects the new cases with no plan change (T8). The G5 and G6 cases build their bus in an error zone of their own, so 'reaches no zone handler' is an assertion rather than a reliance on testWidgets failing on uncaught errors.
